questions.question: Which two sings should be interchanged in the following equation to make it correct? 10 + 5 ÷ 10 × 8 – 10 = 16
questions.questionHtml:
Which two sings should be interchanged in the following equation to make it correct?

10 + 5 ÷ 10 × 8 – 10 = 16
questions.solution:
Interchanging × and +

\(10 \times 5 \div 10 + 8 - 10 = \frac{{10\; \times 5}}{{10}} - 2\)

5 - 2 ≠ 16

Interchanging – and +

\(10 - 5\; \div 10 \times 8 + 10 = 10 - \frac{{5 \times 8}}{{10}} + 10\)

10 - 4 + 10 = 16

Interchanging ÷ and ×

\(10 + 5 \times 10 \div 8 - 10 = 10 + \frac{{50}}{8} - 10\)

\(\frac{{25}}{4} \ne 16\)

Interchanging + and ÷

10 ÷ 5 + 10 × 8 - 10 = 2 + 80 - 10

82 - 10 ≠ 16

Hence we get correct equation by interchanging - and +.

questions.question: Select the number-pair in which the two numbers are related in the same way as are the two numbers of the following number-pair. 7 : 32
questions.questionHtml:
Select the number-pair in which the two numbers are related in the same way as are the two numbers of the following number-pair.

7 : 32
questions.solution:
The pattern followed here is:

Number × [ (Number + 1) ÷ 2 ] + { (Number + 1) ÷ 2 } = RHS

\(7 \times \left[ {\left( {7 + 1} \right) \div 2} \right] + \left[ {\left( {7 + 1} \right) \div 2} \right] = 7 \times 4 + 4 = 32\)

Option 1 :

\(12 \times \left[ {\left( {12 + 1} \right) \div 2} \right] + \left[ {\left( {12 + 1} \right) \div 2} \right] = 12 \times 7.5 + 7.5\; \ne 85\)

Option 2 :

\(16 \times \left[ {\left( {16 + 1} \right) \div 2} \right] + \left[ {\left( {16 + 1} \right) \div 2} \right] = 16 \times 8.5 + 8.5\; \ne 145\)

Option 3 :

\(3 \times \left[ {\left( {3 + 1} \right) \div 2} \right] + \left[ {\left( {3 + 1} \right) \div 2} \right] = 3 \times 2 + 2\; \ne 11\)

Option 4 :

\(13 \times \left[ {\left( {13 + 1} \right) \div 2} \right] + \left[ {\left( {13 + 1} \right) \div 2} \right] = 13 \times 7 + 7 = 98\)

Hence, 13 : 98 is answer.

questions.question: A sum of Rs. 15,000 is lent at 16% p.a. compound interest. What is the difference between the compound interest for the second year and the third year?
questions.questionHtml: A sum of Rs. 15,000 is lent at 16% p.a. compound interest. What is the difference between the compound interest for the second year and the third year?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Interest for 1st year = 16% of 15,000 = 2,400.

Interest for 2nd year = 2,400 + (16% of 2,400) = 2,400 + 384 = 2,784.

The difference between CI of two consecutive years is the interest on the previous year interest.

Difference = 16% of 2,784 = 0.16 × 2,784 = 445.44.

∴ The correct answer is Rs. 445.44.

Alternate Method

Given:

Principal (P) = Rs. 15,000

Rate (R) = 16% p.a.

Formula Used:

Compound Interest for the nth year = P(1 + R/100)n−1 × (R/100)

Calculations:

⇒ CI for 2nd year (CI2) = 15,000 × (1 + 16/100)2−1 × (16/100)

⇒ CI2 = 15,000 × 1.16 × 0.16 = 2,784

⇒ CI for 3rd year (CI3) = 15,000 × (1 + 16/100)3−1 × (16/100)

⇒ CI3 = 15,000 × (1.16)2 × 0.16

⇒ CI3 = 15,000 × 1.3456 × 0.16 = 3,229.44

⇒ Difference = CI3 − CI2 = 3,229.44 − 2,784 = 445.44

∴ The correct answer is Rs. 445.44.

Additional Information

Relationship between Consecutive Year Interests

In compound interest, the interest for the (n+1)th year is equal to the interest for the nth year plus the interest on that interest: CIn+1 = CIn × (1 + R/100).

Difference between CI and SI for 2 years

The difference between Compound Interest and Simple Interest for 2 years is given by the formula: Difference = P × (R/100)2.

Effective Rate for Compound Interest

For two years, the effective rate of interest is x + y + (xy/100). For 16%, it would be 16 + 16 + (256/100) = 34.56%.
